bug_semantics: Four authenticated account operations mutated server-side state while registered as GET routes: /account/follow toggled a follow relationship, /account/delete_notification deleted a notification, /account/mark_notification_read changed one notification's read state, and /account/mark_all_read changed all notifications' read state. Because GET requests were accepted without a CSRF token, a third-party page could induce an authenticated victim's browser to issue a simple request carrying the victim session and perform those mutations.
flaw_origin: Commit 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94 first added all four route decorators and their mutating handlers in website/web/account/account.py, using methods=['GET'] at lines 237, 313, 325, and 335 in that tree. The same commit added GET-based notification callers in website/web/templates/account/account_notifications.html at lines 117, 127, and 138. CSRFProtect was already initialized in website/web/__init__.py, but these state changes were modeled as safe GET requests and therefore bypassed the unsafe-method/token boundary.
ai_marker: present: exact BIC commit-object trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. The same raw commit object identifies both author and committer as `ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>` and contains no bot identity or Generated-with trailer.
evidence: The cited advisory pages https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-75j5-9v4m-c666 and https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-73162 identify CWE-352, name the four GET endpoints, explain the authenticated cross-site request path, and cite the first-party fix https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/commit/c352c2329e48ccc33a2b96d5353450cfbf7e89ec. Both advisory records report affected and patched versions as unknown rather than declaring a package range.

`git log -S` for each exact GET route decorator in website/web/account/account.py independently returned 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94 as the addition and c352c2329e48ccc33a2b96d5353450cfbf7e89ec as the removal. In the BIC tree, `git grep -n` locates methods=['GET'] at website/web/account/account.py:237 (/follow), :313 (/delete_notification), :325 (/mark_notification_read), and :335 (/mark_all_read).

The BIC diff against its immediate parent 45874f5d162c4dc640f1763cb9916bccaf62b261 adds the four GET decorators together with the state-mutating AccountModel calls. A whole-parent-tree `git grep` for /account/follow, /account/delete_notification, /account/mark_notification_read, and /account/mark_all_read returned no matches, proving the vulnerable endpoint lines and paths absent in the direct parent rather than moved from another file.

The exact raw BIC commit object (`git cat-file commit 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94`) has one parent, human author/committer ecrou-exact, and the exact Claude co-author trailer quoted in ai_marker. The first-party commit page https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/commit/4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94 shows the same one-parent 12-file change; https://api.github.com/repos/MISP/cti-transmute/commits/4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94/pulls returned an empty list, so there is no associated PR/member history to decompose and no evidence that this public commit is a squash aggregate.

The direct fix parent f99b996c19faa77f6a65ef61c34c53ade82e9096 still has all four methods=['GET'] decorators at website/web/account/account.py:342, :461, :473, and :483. Commit c352c2329e48ccc33a2b96d5353450cfbf7e89ec changes them respectively to POST, DELETE, POST, and POST and updates every first-party fetch caller to use that method with an X-CSRFToken header; the fixed tree has those methods at the same four source lines.

Repository tag history establishes the tagged version boundary omitted by the advisory: `git tag --contains 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94` returns v1.3, v1.4, and v1.5, while `git tag --contains c352c2329e48ccc33a2b96d5353450cfbf7e89ec` returns only v1.5. Direct tree inspection finds no affected routes in v1.2, all four as GET in v1.3 and v1.4, and POST/DELETE in v1.5. Thus the vulnerable tagged releases are v1.3-v1.4 and the first fixed tagged release is v1.5.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle is direct: 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94 created new follow and notification features and exposed their state mutations through GET; its direct parent contains none of the endpoint paths. Exact-string history shows no earlier writer and no intervening removal/reintroduction, so this source commit—not a later cleanup, move, release, or the security patch—is the smallest public BIC. Its introduction falls after v1.2 and is present in v1.3/v1.4; c352c2329e48ccc33a2b96d5353450cfbf7e89ec directly replaces the unsafe methods and adds CSRF headers before v1.5. AI attribution is judged only from the proven BIC's raw commit object, whose explicit Claude Sonnet 4.6 Co-Authored-By trailer attributes AI participation to the very commit that first wrote the flawed mechanism. That satisfies AI_ROOT_CAUSE rather than relying on later AI work, a PR body, or the fix commit.
